gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's own spec pages give the 16-inch MacBook Pro two external displays on the 2021 M1 Pro and three on today's M5 Pro, all over native USB-C DisplayPort, or that a 16-inch 2560x1600 144 Hz portable needs the USB-C cable rather than HDMI for both its top refresh rate and variable refresh on a Mac.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac portable-monitor roundup and PCWorld's roundup, both read in full, and TechRadar's roundup, which came back truncated after its first pick. RTINGS returned only navigation, so it was not compared. Macworld already states the one-monitor limit on plain M1/M2 Macs, the Trio 3 Pro's software requirement and the Float 2 Pro's 65 W pass-through. PCWorld explains DisplayPort Alt Mode in general terms. Neither gives the external-display count for a 16-inch MacBook Pro by generation, Apple's 'Do not use an HDMI cable or adapter' line for Adaptive Sync, the mini-HDMI refresh cap, or the 65 W pass-through set against the 16-inch's 140 W adapter and separate MagSafe 3 port.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. On a 16-inch MacBook Pro the native one-cable USB-C path is available for every freestanding or stacked single screen in the line, so no driver is needed and the ranking can rest on refresh, brightness and weight. The UPERFECT GR16EQ's 144 Hz and FreeSync are reachable only over USB-C (Steam Flow's review on UPERFECT's blog; Apple's Adaptive Sync page), so the page should tell the shopper to use a Thunderbolt port, not the MacBook's HDMI port. The Duex Float 2 Pro keeps the stacked-above-the-MacBook segment. Its 65 W pass-through is 46% of Apple's 140 W adapter, so the shopper should charge by MagSafe 3 and give the screen its own Thunderbolt port. No maker product page opened today (HTTP 429 on every try), so no price and no maker-page spec is in this file.

findings.label: External displays a current 16-inch MacBook Pro drives (Apple)
findings.value: M5 Pro: up to three external displays; M5 Max: up to four; each up to 6K at 60 Hz or 4K at 144 Hz, over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI ports
findings.note: Apple's page offers the 16-inch only with M5 Pro or M5 Max. A 2560x1600 120 Hz or 144 Hz panel sits inside Apple's stated 4K at 144 Hz ceiling (my comparison, not Apple's wording).

findings.label: Ports and charging on the current 16-inch MacBook Pro (Apple)
findings.value: Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports, one HDMI port, a separate MagSafe 3 charging port; 140 W USB-C Power Adapter included; 100 Wh battery (99.6 Wh actual per Apple's footnote)
findings.note: Charging by MagSafe 3 leaves all three Thunderbolt ports free for a screen, so pass-through charging through the monitor is optional on this laptop.

findings.label: The MacBook Pro 16's own screen (Apple), the match target
findings.value: 16.2-inch, 3456 x 2234 at 254 ppi, ProMotion adaptive refresh up to 120 Hz, up to 1000 nits sustained XDR brightness
findings.note: Source for the page's breakpoint sentence on 120 Hz.

findings.label: External displays the 2021 16-inch MacBook Pro drives (Apple)
findings.value: M1 Pro: up to two external displays up to 6K at 60 Hz; M1 Max: up to three up to 6K plus one up to 4K at 60 Hz. Thunderbolt 4 carries native DisplayPort output over USB-C. The HDMI port supports one display up to 4K at 60 Hz.
findings.note: The oldest Apple-silicon 16-inch already drives two external displays natively, so Macworld's one-monitor limit for plain M1/M2 Macs does not apply to it. Apple states this page's limits at 60 Hz; it does not state a 120 Hz external figure for the 2021 model. A 140 W adapter and MagSafe 3 are also listed here.

findings.label: External-display count depends on the Mac model (Apple)
findings.value: Apple states the number of external displays 'depends on your Mac model' and links a page per model group
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Published November 5, 2026. The page itself carries no per-model counts; I opened only the 2021 and current spec pages.

findings.label: Variable refresh (Adaptive Sync / FreeSync) on a Mac: required path (Apple)
findings.value: macOS Monterey 12 or later and any Mac with Apple silicon; connect to the Thunderbolt port with a Thunderbolt, USB-C or other DisplayPort-enabled cable; 'Do not use an HDMI cable or adapter.'
findings.source_title: Use an Adaptive Sync external display with your Mac - Apple Support
findings.note: Published July 16, 2026. Turned on in System Settings > Displays > Refresh Rate > Variable or Adaptive. Apple adds 'Check with the display manufacturer for Adaptive Sync compatibility with your Mac' and says to turn it off if the display flickers.

findings.label: Refresh rate by input (Steam Flow review, published on UPERFECT's blog)
findings.value: 144 Hz over USB-C; the Mini HDMI input 'caps out at 130 Hz at this resolution' (2560 x 1600)
findings.source_title: UPERFECT GR16EQ monitor review (Steam Flow), UPERFECT blog
findings.note: Dated June 30, 2026. UPERFECT sent the unit and hosts the review, so treat it as maker-adjacent. Tested on a Steam Deck, not a Mac. The reviewer says 'Any device that supports display port out mode over USB-C will get the same experience.'

findings.label: Ports, FreeSync and box contents (Steam Flow review on UPERFECT's blog)
findings.value: Two full-featured USB-C ports, one mini HDMI, 3.5 mm audio jack; rated 144 Hz with FreeSync; box holds two USB-C cables and a 20 W charging brick; no HDMI cable is listed in the review
findings.source_title: UPERFECT GR16EQ monitor review (Steam Flow), UPERFECT blog
findings.note: The reviewer calls the included USB-C cables short. He also says some docks and handhelds 'won't get VRR enabled'.

findings.label: Brightness on bus power (Steam Flow review, Steam Deck as host)
findings.value: Defaults to 30% brightness each time when powered only by the Steam Deck; 'You need the charging brick plugged in to get the full brightness and save your settings.'
findings.source_title: UPERFECT GR16EQ monitor review (Steam Flow), UPERFECT blog
findings.note: Measured on a Steam Deck's USB-C port, not a MacBook Pro's Thunderbolt port. Whether a MacBook Pro port lifts this limit is not sourced, so the page should not state the rated brightness as available on one cable without the brick.

findings.label: Panel, ports and pass-through (Macworld)
findings.value: 16-inch 2560 x 1600 at 120 Hz; USB-C and Mini HDMI; 65 W pass-through charging; $299.99 when Macworld reviewed it
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 - Macworld
findings.note: Macworld is a cited rival, so this is not new. Arithmetic: 65 W / 140 W (Apple's included adapter) = 46%. The Macworld price is a review-time figure, not today's store price.

findings.label: Attachment to the laptop (Macworld)
findings.value: 'You can keep it physically attached to your laptop with the included magnets but this is an option rather than a necessity.'
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 - Macworld
findings.note: It stands on its own behind the MacBook, so the stacked position does not depend on fixing magnets to the lid.

findings.label: One-external-display limit on base Macs (Macworld)
findings.value: 'Note that plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs plus the new MacBook Neo are limited to connecting just a single monitor.'
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 - Macworld
findings.note: Rival already states this. It does not add that the 2021 and current 16-inch MacBook Pro come only with Pro or Max chips (Apple spec pages above).

findings.label: Video path on a Mac (Macworld)
findings.value: 'To work with the Trio 3 Pro users of those Macs will need to download and install free software (rather like DisplayLink)'; Macworld lists 'compatible with 13-16-inch MacBooks'
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 - Macworld
findings.note: 'Those Macs' are the single-monitor base models. The Trio 3 Pro's panels are 14.1-inch, so it is outside this page's 16-inch line.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex Float (original, not the 2 Pro)
findings.label: Video path (Mobile Pixels FAQ)
findings.value: 'Duex Float is plug-and-play If your computer has a USB-C port with DisplayPort enabled'; otherwise HDMI to mini-HDMI plus a non-DP USB port for power; draws 7 W max
findings.note: This FAQ covers the original 15.6-inch 1080p Duex Float only. It does not mention the Float 2 Pro, 120 Hz or pass-through charging, so it is a lead on the family's video path, not a Float 2 Pro spec.

findings.label: One-cable requirement as Mobile Pixels states it
findings.value: 'A portable monitor should therefore support USB-C DisplayPort Alt-Mode so video, data, and up to 15 W power can ride a single cable.'
findings.source_title: How to Choose the Best Portable Monitor for Your MacBook Pro - Mobile Pixels
findings.note: Dated September 10, 2025, by Jime Chen. The 15 W figure is Mobile Pixels' statement, not Apple's. The article names the Duex Float and Duex Max DS, both 1080p, and does not name the Float 2 Pro.
